newsitem.title: FRANCE: Britain to rejoin UNESCO under Labour.
newsitem.headline: Britain to rejoin UNESCO under Labour.

text.p: The new Labour government is to bring Britain back into UNESCO which it left 12 years ago, complaining of mismanagement and a Third Word slant, new British Foreign Secretary Robin Cook was quoted as saying on Tuesday.

British diplomatic sources quoted Cook, whose party ended 18 years of rule by the Conservative party this month, as telling fellow European foreign ministers that "Britain will carry out its long-standing commitment to return to UNESCO".

Cook was attending a meeting of the Western European Union (WEU) defence body gathering foreign and defence ministers from 28 European countries at the Paris headquarters of UNESCO, the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organisation.

The United States and Britain, two major contributors to UNESCO, left the organisation in 1985, complaining of wasted resources and excessive politicisation under the directorship of Amadou Mahtar M'Bow.
They also opposed attempts to create a new world information order boosting the role of government-controlled news media.
Spain's Federico Mayor took over from M'Bow two years later, carrying out a reorganisation to make spending more efficient.
The British diplomatic sources said that radical reforms had been made in the running of UNESCO, and it was now carrying out important work in which Britain wanted to be involved.
Washington has indicated it is considering rejoining UNESCO, but a spokeswoman for the organisation said no concrete step had been taken, partly because of U.S. budget problems.
